How to play & keyboard shortcuts

Every sticker has its own solid-color dot, grouped with its current face.

Restore each face to a single color. Select one of the eight turn sides, then drag along its ring or use Ring left / Ring right. The two sides of an axis (L/l, R/r, D/d, B/b) use the same central cut and rotate opposite halves of the puzzle.

Every node is one actual sticker, in one solid color. Connected rings show the sticker paths for every rotation axis. The selected axis stays bright while the other rings remain visible. Click any ring to select it, then drag along its path to turn. “Focus selected rings” dims the other axes without removing them.

Drag the 3D puzzle to look around; scroll or pinch to zoom. Click a visible axis letter to select that side. “Piece labels” shows each piece’s home name and, after an arrow, its current slot. Rotate the view to expose labels hidden at the edges. The puzzle has four physical rotation axes with eight directed turn sides. Its placement in the Octahedral collection follows this site’s eight-side family labels.

Use ←/→ for the selected ring. Letter keys L, R, D, B turn the main sides; hold Shift for the inverse. Use the on-screen lowercase buttons for the opposite sides. A prime (′) means counterclockwise viewed inward along that axis. With the 3D view focused, arrow keys rotate the camera and +/− zoom.

Randomize continues from the current position and applies 24 legal turns using a fresh random seed. Auto solve opens the Constrained Solver and works from the current arrangement, pausing between stages and highlighting solved nodes that later stages protect. It does not need recorded moves or promise the shortest solution; difficult states may reach the computation limit. Pause stops the current sequence, and Reset returns immediately to solved. Your state stays in this browser tab.
